status: Fluree v4.2.0: 105/105 queries, 17.5 ms geometric mean; QLever 202.4 ms and Virtuoso 299.7 ms. Native engines on matching m7a.4xlarge hardware, using the same DBLP snapshot and 105 queries.

dataset.name: DBLP-core (bibliography only)
dataset.description: Standard DBLP RDF bibliography, no OpenCitations citations — DROPS monthly archive 2026-06-01

methodology.notes: Local HTTP, TSV responses, no result cache. One warmup and median of three measured requests, with a 180 s timeout and timed-query wall budget. QLever result cache disabled and cleared per query. QLever and Virtuoso used 300 s caps, but no query finished between 180 and 300 s. Oxigraph uses the single-run protocol described below.

fluree.label: Fluree
fluree.config: Official x86_64 Linux release binary, checksum verified. Fresh native import; default auto cache and Sync durability. Local HTTP TSV; no result cache.

import.notes: fluree create dblp --from dblp.nt; 561,477,456 distinct statements. Process wall time includes import completion and statistics; single import measurement.

qlever.label: QLever
qlever.commit: 621cf31 (native binaries from adfreiburg/qlever:latest image, run directly — no Docker)
qlever.config: native; MEMORY_FOR_QUERIES 26G, CACHE_MAX_SIZE 6G (disabled for the benchmark), in-memory-compressed vocab, TIMEOUT 300s — matches ad-freiburg/sparqloscope docs/Qleverfile.dblp

import.notes: qlever index (native), parallel parse @ 2.3 M/s. in-memory-compressed vocab, num-triples-per-batch 1M (matches the paper). Native on the host needed two things Docker masked: ulimit -n raised to 1048576 (533 partial vocabs) and --stxxl-memory 20G (permutation merge). Loaded 561,477,456 distinct triples.
import.phases: parse 247 s @ 2.3 M/s + vocab merge + convert + sort/permutations; total 521 s

oxigraph.label: Oxigraph
oxigraph.config: serve-read-only; systemd MemoryMax 52G; no result cache; no server-side query timeout (issue #1336). Sweep methodology DEVIATES from the other engines: warmup 0 + 1 timed run, 180 s timeout, memory-capped with per-query restart-on-failure (mirrors ad-freiburg/sparqloscope util/oxigraph-helper.sh). RocksDB-backed.

import.notes: oxigraph load --format nt --lenient. Till-ready = 329 s parse @ 1.70 M t/s + ~243 s RocksDB compaction. Loaded 561,477,456 triples. No COUNT fastpath. 39/105 queries completed within 180 s; 66/105 timed out.
import.phases: parse 329 s @ 1.70 M t/s + RocksDB compaction ~243 s = 572 s till-ready

virtuoso.label: Virtuoso
virtuoso.config: 32 GB profile: NumberOfBuffers 2,720,000 (~21 GB), MaxDirtyBuffers 2,000,000, MaxQueryExecutionTime 300 s, ResultSetMaxRows 10M. Data in named graph <https://dblp.org>; queries sent with default-graph-uri. Ubuntu apt 07.20.3229 has a broken ld_dir; data loaded via chunked TTLP(file_to_string(chunk)) in parallel.

import.notes: split -l 50000 + 8 parallel TTLP threads + checkpoint. Loaded 561,483,067 triples, 90 predicates. number-of-objects timed out (>180 s full distinct scan); transitive-path-plus returned engine error. 103/105 completed.
import.phases: chunked TTLP load + checkpoint = ~700 s till-ready

millenniumdb.label: MillenniumDB
millenniumdb.config: native; versioned-buffer 22GB, strings-static 4GB, strings-dynamic 4GB; body POST; no result cache. Built on its own m7a.4xlarge (16c/64GB), dblp-core pulled from S3.

import.notes: mdb import --format ttl --buffer-strings 20GB --buffer-tensors 20GB (scaled down from the paper's 40GB+40GB=80GB, which OOMs a 64GB box). Loaded 561,477,456 triples, 90 predicates. number-of-objects/number-of-subjects timed out (>180 s full distinct scans); 103/105 completed.

jena.label: Jena
jena.config: TDB2 + Fuseki; JVM_ARGS -Xmx32g; body POST; no result cache. Fuseki started cold for benchmark run (no JVM warmup, no OS page cache warmup of 54GB index).

import.notes: tdb2.xloader (external-sort bulk loader). Loaded from 574.2M-line .nt. TDB index pre-built; Fuseki started cold for benchmark. Cold 54GB index + no COUNT fastpath caused 71/105 timeouts; only 34/105 completed.
import.phases: nodes 1217 s + terms + data + per-permutation index build = 7471 s till-ready

blazegraph.label: Blazegraph
blazegraph.config: native jar; offline DataLoader on a SKOLEMIZED .nt (blank nodes rewritten to IRIs — required: default load silently drops ALL blank-node triples, 239M/561M); served with -Xmx16g; web.xml queryTimeout 180000; queries via --post-form. Dedicated m7a.4xlarge.

import.notes: REQUIRED skolemization: default load silently drops all blank-node triples (239M/561M). Skolemizing _:label -> IRI then DataLoader gave the full 561,544,658. +~33 min skolemize (sed) before the 9950 s load.
import.phases: skolemize ~33 min + DataLoader 9950 s (2.76 h) = ~3.3 h till-ready

caveats: Fluree measured 2026-09-07; other engines measured 2026-06-11. Dedicated hosts of the same instance class, not the same physical host. Absolute timings can vary between hosts.
All engines use the pinned 2026-06-01 DBLP archive. This differs from the older snapshots used in the SPARQLoscope paper, so absolute timings are not directly comparable to that paper.
Virtuoso uses chunked TTLP loading; its ld_dir loader was broken in the tested Ubuntu package.
Jena starts with a cold JVM/TDB cache and a 54 GB index on a 64 GB host; its completion count is cache-state sensitive.
Oxigraph uses no warmup and one measured request, with a 180 s timeout, a memory cap, and restart on failure. This differs from the other engines' warmup/median-of-three protocol.
This comparison measures query completion and latency. It does not assert result equivalence across all engines. See the per-query table for differences in performance.
[Reproduce the Fluree run](v420-release/REPORT.md): pinned binary, dataset and harness checksums, import and query commands.
